note.seg: strub. Sc Hg [etwa verlesen aus scublum, das die Vorlage latinisirt hätte aus scobl: ‘Schaufel’, vgl. Brunner DRG. II 270]
strub. Sc Hg [perhaps misread from scublum, which the exemplar would have Latinised from scobl: ‘shovel’, cf. Brunner DRG. II 270]

vgl. Brunner DRG. II 270 und im 11. Jh. Durhamer Wiederfreilassung von früher Selbstversklarten: þa men þe heo nam heora heafod for hyra mete on þam yflum dagum ‘Menschen, deren Haupt sie [die Freilasserin] genommen hatte, wegen deren Ernährung in den bösen Zeiten’; ed. Earle Landcharters 275

cf. Brunner DRG. II 270 and, in the 11th cent., the Durham re-manumission of persons who had earlier enslaved themselves: þa men þe heo nam heora heafod for hyra mete on þam yflum dagum ‘people whose heads she [the manumitter] had taken on account of their food in the evil times’; ed. Earle Landcharters 275

Ähnlich Westgotisch-Castilianisch; Palgrave Rise of Engl. commonw. I 23. Houards Erklärung (Cout. Agnorm. I 348) strublum: ‘couteaux’ scheint falsch. Beim Pflügen treibt man Zugochsen cum stimulo: mid gadisene; Wright-Wülcker Glossar. I 90. Mistgabel und Dreschflegel sind anderwärts Symbole des Bauern im Ggs. zum Ritter; Vinogradoff Villainage 170—in{35} m. überspr. Rs

Similarly in Visigothic-Castilian law; Palgrave Rise of Engl. commonw. I 23. Houard’s explanation (Cout. Agnorm. I 348) of strublum as ‘couteaux’ seems wrong. In ploughing, draught oxen are driven cum stimulo: mid gadisene; Wright-Wülcker Glossar. I 90. Elsewhere the dung-fork and the flail are symbols of the peasant in contrast to the knight; Vinogradoff Villainage 170—in{35} m. omitted Rs
